narrative.overview:
Uncached is a calm, grounded instrument for a risky task. Its dark evergreen canvas makes the workspace feel protected, while pale sage signals safe forward motion. The interface is deliberately quiet: it gives scanning, review, and confirmation enough room to be understood without turning cleanup into a spectacle.

The system uses soft edges and restrained texture to make developer tooling feel approachable without becoming playful. Technical information such as paths, categories, and sizes uses a distinct monospace voice; action and explanation remain humanist and readable.
keyCharacteristics: Deep evergreen canvas with layered forest surfaces.
Pale botanical green for safe, affirmative actions.
Soft coral for destructive or cancelling actions.
Rounded, tactile controls with compact developer-tool density.
Quiet motion that clarifies transitions and progress.

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Sage and coral are state signals, not decoration. Use them where users need to understand what is safe, active, selected, cancelling, or destructive.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Humanist type explains and invites; monospace type identifies filesystem facts. Do not use mono for general prose.

rules.name: The Grounded Surface Rule
rules.body: Cards and controls sit in the forest layers. Do not float every element with a shadow; reserve lift for modal interruption and meaningful focus.

dos: Do preserve Deep Forest surfaces and use tonal contrast before adding decoration.
Do reserve Fresh Sage for safe action, progress, selection, and focus.
Do use Geist Mono for paths, categories, counts, and other filesystem facts.
Do keep destructive actions unmistakably Coral and explicit.
Do respect reduced-motion preferences and keep transitions short.
donts: Don't introduce generic neon gradients, cyberpunk glow, or terminal-green spectacle.
Don't use coral as a general accent or interchangeable brand color.
Don't make every container shadowed or floating.
Don't turn technical metadata into decorative typography.
Don't replace the Uncached logo assets with improvised marks.
